paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage: opinions about Jesus are everywhere, and they don't all fit. His family says, "He is out of His mind," and the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem say, "He is possessed by Beelzebul" (Mark 3:21-22). Jesus doesn't ignore it, He answers with "How can Satan drive out Satan?" (Mark 3:23). So the lesson for you, baker, is to measure Jesus by what He says and does, not by the loudest voice in the room.

Jesus shows what's really going on: a divided kingdom or house "cannot stand," and no one steals from a strong man's house "unless he first ties up the strong man" (Mark 3:24-27). I take that to mean Jesus isn't working with the enemy, He's the One stronger than him. Then comes the heavy part: whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit "will never be forgiven," and Mark tells us why He said it: they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit" (Mark 3:29-30). I think this is a serious warning about calling the work of the Spirit something evil, so let's take it seriously and not toss it around.

Then His mother and brothers are standing outside, and Jesus asks, "Who are My mother and My brothers?" (Mark 3:33). He looks at the people sitting around Him and says, "whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother" (Mark 3:35). That means you, baker: the way in is doing the will of God, not who your people are or where you come from. I know a little about being stuck in a drawer, so believe me, being family to Jesus is the best seat in the house!
